problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=x(t)+\frac{1}{2}y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-2x(t)-y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear differential equations above. The eigenvector corresponding to the only eigenvalue $\lambda =0$ of the system's matrix $A$ is $v=[-1,\text{ }2]^{T}.$ The vector $w=[-1,\text{ }0]^{T}$ is such that $(A-\lambda I)w=v.$  Which of the following could represent the phase portrait of the system?

*Hint: Here, the dotted line represents the equilibrium solutions.*
worked_solution:
Since we have a repeated eigenvalue $\lambda =0$ (of multiplicity two) and only one corresponding eigenvector $v,$ the solution of the system is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}v{e}^{\lambda t}+{c}_{2}(vt{e}^{\lambda t}+w{e}^{\lambda t}\,),
$$

where $w$ is a solution to the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v.$

In our case, 

$$
\lambda =0,\,v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

 
Thus, the general solution of the system is

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}] & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]) \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-t-1 \\ 2t\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.\end{aligned}
$$

First, notice that ${x}_{E}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ are equilibrium solutions of the system since ${x}_{E}^{′}(t)=0.$ These solutions form the line with the equation $y=-2x$ in the phase space, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14069892/assets/6044d391016e37af929b36e89e0a802151b5710707cc510e9e7f70bf9a2d1c0d.png)

Now, we consider some general solutions of the form 

$$
[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-t-1 \\ 2t\end{aligned}].
$$

For example:

- When ${c}_{1}=1$ and ${c}_{2}=1,$ we get the following curve: 

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-t-2 \\ y=2t+2\end{aligned}
$$

Let's add it to the phase space:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14069892/assets/54bdfaf14b4f580e1476d4649e03cd71cb8203e23ae318daa65251fd7ce02ba1.png)

- When ${c}_{1}=-1$ and ${c}_{2}=-1,$ we get the following curve: 

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=t+2 \\ y=-2t-2\end{aligned}
$$

Let's add it to the phase space:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14069892/assets/edb5558ed7b5ee0e4aacb4eb67d74747fcc366f1508e16b3e99f3e0d5ee53306.png)

The phase portrait of our system looks as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14069892/assets/1005575ad1d73527ce1bd4e946aa9a3d0be86ae82329fde27700082ea2b5c121.png)
